column1: # OFFSCREEN AGENDAS -- what an NPC is doing about a loop while the party is elsewhere.
# Append-only. One row per EVENT: `open`, `pause`, `resume`, `close`. What is active is
# DERIVED from the latest row for each id. tools/offscreen.py reads this and rolls the
# ticks; tools/log.py `day` runs it on every new campaign day.
# THE TABLE IS WRITTEN HERE BEFORE THE FIRST ROLL, which is the same "declared first"
# kinds: progress (something moved) | hold (nothing yet) | resolve (done, the agenda closes
# itself) | due (a fixed obligation). `auto|due:text` has no die. Cadence is in campaign days
# (the player set weekly, day 135). Ceiling is the most ticks it will ever run; after that it
# THE NEWS IS HIDDEN UNTIL THE PARTY MEETS THE PERSON (player, day 135): `offscreen.py news
# --who NAME`, then `deliver`. Roll results go to rolls.tsv like every other roll.
# NO MANUFACTURED URGENCY: a tick may move, hold or finish a thing already in the record. It
# does not invent a new problem.

column8: Answers to Wend's four letters to the holders about next season's price (due before shearing)
column9: d6|1-2=progress:One of the four holders has answered Wend. WHICH holder and WHAT he understood about the price is the DM's to author when Wend tells the party.|3-6=hold:No holder has answered yet.

column8: Osk's answer to the cart-hire sheet (a flat rate a load, his name on the contract)
column9: d6|1-2=progress:Osk has answered the cart-hire sheet. YES or NO, and his terms, are the DM's to author when Wend tells the party.|3-6=hold:Osk has not answered.

column8: Who in Ludbury is saying the art. 7 floor is unfair, and why
column9: d6|1=progress:Wend has learned something more about who in Ludbury is saying the wool floor is unfair. WHAT is the DM's to author when she tells the party.|2-6=hold:Nothing new on the Ludbury rumour.

column8: Flax on Gyll's four-and-a-bit acres: ask the eleven, one at a time, and nobody goes near Gyll first (Ottir's condition); the seed at Marchford is a spring job
column9: d6|1-3=progress:Wend has put the question about Gyll's field to one more of the eleven, quietly, as Ottir's condition requires. WHO and WHAT he said are the DM's to author when she tells the party. Nothing has been sown: flax is a spring crop.|4-6=hold:Wend has not got to the eleven this week: the barn, the holders and the wool come first.

column8: The wall at Wend's barn pointed with the party's mortar and rope before the frost
column9: d6|1-2=resolve:Coll has pointed the barn wall with the party's mortar and used the rope on the job. It is done.|3-6=progress:Coll's crew has got part of the wall done between other work; the rest is in hand.

column8: Toller's six correspondents in six towns: word from Ossery and the Ludbury man
column9: d6|1=progress:Toller has heard from one of his correspondents (Ossery at Marchford or the Ludbury man). WHAT is the DM's to author when Toller tells the party.|2-6=hold:No word from Toller's correspondents this week.

column8: Toller's date-work on the area 6 papers and the 86 marks, now that the barrels are opened and their contents known
column9: d6|1-2=progress:Toller has made more of the papers by comparing the marks with what the barrels actually held. WHAT he has found is the DM's to author when he tells the party.|3-6=hold:Toller has not got further with the papers this week.

column8: Holt's monthly coin on the first market day, on the goods account (40 gp, and the tab runs beside it)
column9: auto|due:Holt's 40 gp in coin falls due on the first market day of the month. The Inn tab has run beside it in the nights the party slept there.

column8: Halm's readiness for the next run (his cart and mule, 8 sp a day)
column9: d6|1-2=progress:Halm has taken a small carting job of his own and his cart is out for a few days. The DM authors how long when the party asks.|3-6=hold:Halm's cart and mule stand ready.
